messages:
maria: Customer Brightline reported a sudden embeddings throughput drop — tokens/sec looks normal (~2.5k t/s) but vectors/sec is down ~70%. They also see 128-d vectors intermittently where they expect 1536. Happened around 09:08 PST.

devon: Can you paste a failing request/response and a req id? Any HTTP errors?

maria: No 5xxs, 200 OK. Example req id: req_0a9f2. Client receives embeddings with length 128. Repro curl they used:

curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"openembed-1536","input":["sample text"],"batch_size":64}'

maria: Response body (trimmed): {"data":[{"embedding":[0.001,...],"length":128}],"model":"openembed-1536"}

alex: That smells like a routing fallback to a smaller/quantized variant. Check router logs for X-Model-Variant and kvcache metrics for that req id. Also check GPU queue_depth and batcher logs.

samir: Looking at infra metrics around 09:06-09:10: GPU util on node gpu-07 peaked at 96-99%, batcher.queue_depth spiked to ~180, and kvcache_hit_rate dropped ~15%. PromQL snapshots attached in logs.

sre-bot: [alert] autoscaler: pod scale-down due to mem pressure at 09:07:41. New pods booted with model variant mapping table that includes 'openembed-1536-quant' as compatible fallback.

devon: If the platform allows cross-variant fallbacks we should guarantee output dims. This sounds like a bug where fallback returned vectors from a different model without updating metadata.

maria: Support note: customer-side validation expects 1536 dims; they don't gracefully handle mismatches and started throwing client-side errors after the first mismatch. Impact: Brightline ingestion pipeline stalled.

alex: Repro steps for eng to reproduce locally: 1) send 1k concurrent embedding requests with batch_size=64 to model=openembed-1536 in us-west-2 2) instrument router to log X-Model-Variant 3) observe vectors/sec vs tokens/sec ratio and any variant changes. Example load script snippet:

for i in {1..1000}; do \
  jq -n --arg s "text $i" '{model:"openembed-1536",input:[$s],batch_size:64}' | \
  curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @- &
  sleep 0.01
done

samir: From node logs (req_0a9f2.log): router.selected_variant=openembed-384-quant, router.reason="capacity_fallback", batcher.queue_depth=142, kvcache.lock_wait_ms=87.

maria: Support asked customer to temporarily pin model_version in their request. They also enabled client-side dim check to drop mismatched vectors until we fix.

devon: Immediate mitigations: 1) Add a safety check in router to never change model name reported in response headers if dims differ (fail instead), 2) add alert when vectors/sec / tokens/sec < 0.6 for a project. Opening ENG ticket.

alex: Longer-term: make fallback variants dim-compatible or ensure router rewrites model field in the API response to reflect actual variant and expose X-Model-Variant header. Also revisit autoscaler policy that caused unexpected pod churn.

samir: Temporary infra action: increasing dedicated burst capacity for the affected customer and reducing max_batch_size from 64 -> 32 to lower queue depth. Rolling deploy to us-west-2 in ~15m.

maria: Support escalated to P1 and informed Brightline of the mitigation steps. They've accepted pinning for now. Please track fixes in ENG-4581.

devon: Queries to attach to ticket: 
- vectors/sec vs tokens/sec ratio: sum(rate(embeddings_vectors_generated_total[1m])) / sum(rate(tokens_generated_total[1m]))
- batcher queue depth: max(batcher_queue_depth{job="batcher"})
- kvcache hold/wait: increase in kvcache_lock_wait_ms

alex: I'll add a temporary dashboard and an alert rule for vector/token ratio drop. Also adding a router invariant test to CI to catch mismatched-dim fallbacks.

maria: Thanks all. I'll keep this thread updated with customer replies and re-open if we see recurrence. :thumbsup:
